newsitem.title: UK: C-S refutes Virgin anti-competitive claim.
newsitem.headline: C-S refutes Virgin anti-competitive claim.

text.p: Cadbury-Schweppes refuted claims made by Virgin Cola that it is abusing its dominant position in the UK cola market.

"We note that Virgin intends making a formal complaint to the EC alleging anti-competitive practice by CCSB (Coca-Cola Schweppes & Beverages) in the UK cola market," said a spokeswoman for Cadbury-Schweppes.
"We would point out that these allegations seem to ignore the findings of the UK Monopolies and Mergers Commission inquiry in 1991 into the UK carbonated soft drinks market."
CCSB, 51 percent owned by Cadbury-Schweppes, is currently the subject of a European Commission inquiry into Cadbury's proposed sale of its stake to Coca-Cola Enterprises.

The MMC made no adverse findings about the home trade after a year long investigation and CCSB changed its "practices regarding range discounts and exclusive agreements in on premise trade following the MMC recommendations," said the spokeswoman.

"The European Commission was closely consulted when the MMC undertook this inquiry," she added. "We believe that the beverages market in the UK is very competitive and will continue to be very competitive after this deal goes through. We are continuing to co-operate with the commission in its inquiry and remain confident that the proposed sale of CCSB will be completed in January."
CCSB adds water to concentrate, carbonates and bottles and distributes a range of soft drinks.
